events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I'll check what's in the workspace first.

events.content:
I've built the book tracker as a small Node app with no extra dependencies. It saves books to data/books.json, and the tests (npm test) pass: 5 of 5. A quick run of the real server also worked: adding a book redirected back to the home page, the book appeared in the list, and it was written to the JSON file.

To run it: npm start, then open http://127.0.0.1:3000.

- Home page: shows "Currently reading" and "Finished" lists, with a form at the bottom to add a book (title, author, notes).
- Mark finished: each book you're reading has a "Mark finished" button, on the home page and on the book's own page.
- Book page: /books/<id> shows the title, author, whether you're still reading it or when you finished, and your notes. It also shows the full link so you can copy and send it.
- Saving: books are still there after a restart (a test checks this). Each save writes a temp file and swaps it in, so a crash mid-save can't damage the file.
- Safety: empty titles or authors are rejected, anything typed into the form is displayed as plain text rather than run as code, and unknown book links show a "not found" page.

The code is in server.js (starts the app), src/store.js (reads and writes the JSON file), src/app.js (pages and forms) and test/app.test.js. I added the start and test scripts to package.json and added data/ to .gitignore so your reading list isn't committed.

Two things to know about sharing links:
- Where it runs: by default the app only accepts connections from your own computer, so a link you send won't open for anyone else. For that, run it on a machine they can reach, for example with HOST=0.0.0.0 npm start on your network or on a server. PORT changes the port and BOOKS_FILE changes where the data is saved.
- No accounts: anyone who can open the app can also add books or mark them finished, not just view them.
